evidence: Two parallel sets of sidebar panel implementations coexist in crates/colony-ui-core: one under src/builtins/ (FileTreeSidebarComponent, GitFilesSidebarComponent, McpSidebarComponent, SessionSidebarComponent) and one under src/sidebar/panels/ (FileTreePanel, GitFilesPanel, McpPanel, SessionPanel). The builtins variants use SidebarLine as their line type; the panels variants use ComponentLine directly.

The builtins sidebar types use the naming suffix 'SidebarComponent' (e.g. FileTreeSidebarComponent) while the panels directory uses the suffix 'Panel' (e.g. FileTreePanel) for structurally identical things.

colony-filetree-bin/src/main.rs subscribes to the tuple key 'cwd_change' (line 24, 65), while the system emits 'dir_change' everywhere else (colony-exec/src/builtins.rs, colony-ui-core/src/builtins/*.rs, etc.). The comment on line 63 of filetree-bin even reads '// React to dir_change: ...' but the match checks for 'cwd_change'.

colony-filetree-bin uses bare .unwrap() in emit_frame and emit_tuple (lines 35, 105, 118), while the structurally identical colony-env-bin uses .expect() with a message for the same serialization calls (lines 25, 111). This is a direct sibling-protocol inconsistency between two panel binaries.

The file icon mapping function exists in three separate places with diverging extension sets: colony-filetree-bin/src/main.rs (file_icon), colony-ui-core/src/builtins/sidebar_file_tree.rs (file_icon), and colony-ui-core/src/sidebar/panels/file_tree.rs (file_style on FileTreePanel). Each covers slightly different extension sets and uses different icon codepoints for the same extension.

strengths: Prompt component types (PromptComponent implementors) form a consistent family: identical import headers, identical new()/default() pattern, subscriptions() returning Vec<TuplePattern>, render() returning ComponentOutput. Every file in crates/colony-ui-core/src/builtins/ for prompt components follows this without drift.
Naming is uniformly snake_case for functions and PascalCase for types throughout all seed files and their neighbors; there is no camelCase drift anywhere.

The panel binary protocol (sentinel-based stdin/stdout IPC) is coherently structured in both colony-env-bin and colony-filetree-bin, with the same event loop shape, emit_frame helper, and InputEvent matching — the protocol convention is recognizable across sibling binaries.

The tuple key naming convention ('dir_change', 'env_change', 'file_change', 'cmd_complete') is applied consistently across the shell core, ui-core builtins, and subscription modules — the drift is isolated to one binary.
convention_outlier.issue_character: The issues are concentrated in two structural areas: a duplicated subsystem (sidebar panels implemented twice under different directory paths with different type and suffix naming) and a single factual mismatch in a panel binary (wrong subscription key, inconsistent error handling style). They are not pervasive across the codebase but they do create real navigational confusion for anyone working in the UI layer.
convention_outlier.score_rationale: The codebase scores well on in-family consistency — within each area, conventions hold. The drag comes from two intersecting problems: the sidebar subsystem has forked into two locations with different naming conventions (Panel vs SidebarComponent suffix, ComponentLine vs SidebarLine usage), making the ui-core directory non-trivially confusing to navigate. The 'cwd_change' vs 'dir_change' mismatch in colony-filetree-bin means that binary silently never reacts to directory changes — a functional bug rooted in convention drift. This is enough to place the score solidly in the 70-75 range: a developer would trust patterns in one area only to find them contradicted in a nearby sibling subsystem.

issues.summary: Two parallel sidebar panel implementations coexist under builtins/ and sidebar/panels/ with different type names and line types
evidence: FileTreeSidebarComponent in builtins/sidebar_file_tree.rs and FileTreePanel in sidebar/panels/file_tree.rs both implement SidebarComponent for the same 'file_tree' id, but use different line types (SidebarLine vs ComponentLine) and different class-name suffixes.

GitFilesSidebarComponent in builtins/sidebar_git_files.rs and GitFilesPanel in sidebar/panels/git_files.rs both parse git porcelain output and render git file lists independently, with diverging status type enums (GitFileStatus defined in both files with different variant sets: panels version has Staged/Conflict variants the builtins version lacks).
McpSidebarComponent and McpPanel, SessionSidebarComponent and SessionPanel: four pairs of structurally equivalent components across two directories.
issues.suggestion: Determine which implementation is canonical and delete the other. The builtins/ variants use SidebarLine (which has a From<SidebarLine> for ComponentLine conversion already defined) and appear more featureful; the sidebar/panels/ variants use ComponentLine directly. Pick one set, update all callers, and remove the duplicate directory. Do not add an abstraction layer to unify them — simply pick the richer implementation.

issues.summary: colony-filetree-bin subscribes to 'cwd_change' but the system emits 'dir_change'; the binary silently never reacts to directory changes
evidence: colony-exec/src/builtins.rs lines 369, 4239, 4280, 4317, 4395, 6735: all emit `Value::Str("dir_change".to_string())` as the tuple key for directory change events

colony-shell/src/repl_tui.rs line 830: the TUI host broadcasts key 'cwd_change' to panels specifically — this is a separate panel-protocol broadcast path. The tuple-space path uses 'dir_change'. The subscription to 'cwd_change' may be intentional for the panel host path, but the comment on line 63 of filetree-bin reads '// React to dir_change' while the code checks 'cwd_change', indicating at minimum a documentation/convention inconsistency.
issues.suggestion: Audit whether colony-filetree-bin is intended to receive events via the panel-host broadcast path (which does use 'cwd_change') or via the tuple space (which uses 'dir_change'). If panel-host broadcast is the intended path, fix the comment on line 63 to say 'cwd_change'. If tuple space is intended, change the subscription key and matching key from 'cwd_change' to 'dir_change'. Add a constant (e.g. `const KEY_DIR_CHANGE: &str = "dir_change"`) shared across the panel binaries to prevent this class of mismatch.

issues.summary: Sibling panel binaries use different error handling style: colony-env-bin uses .expect() with messages, colony-filetree-bin uses bare .unwrap()
evidence: colony-filetree-bin/src/main.rs line 35: `serde_json::to_string(&config).unwrap()` — bare unwrap, no message
colony-filetree-bin/src/main.rs lines 105, 118: two more bare `.unwrap()` on serialization calls that env-bin treats with .expect()
issues.suggestion: Replace the three bare `.unwrap()` calls in colony-filetree-bin/src/main.rs with `.expect("<msg>")` matching the convention established in colony-env-bin: `serde_json::to_string(&config).expect("config must serialize")`, `serde_json::to_string(&line).expect("frame line must serialize")`, `serde_json::to_string(&emit).expect("tuple emit must serialize")`.

issues.summary: File extension-to-icon mapping is implemented three times independently with diverging extension sets and icon codepoints
evidence: colony-ui-core/src/builtins/sidebar_file_tree.rs defines `fn file_icon(name: &str) -> (&'static str, Color)` covering rs/toml/md/json/js/ts/py/go/sh/bash/zsh/lock/yml/yaml — different icon codepoints for the same extensions, adds Color

colony-ui-core/src/sidebar/panels/file_tree.rs defines `fn file_style(&self, ext: &Option<String>) -> (&'static str, Color)` covering rs/toml/json/yaml/yml/md/txt/sh/bash/zsh/py/js/ts/jsx/tsx/go/c/cpp/h/hpp/html/htm/css/scss/sass/lock — the most complete set, but different codepoints for the same extensions vs the builtins version
issues.suggestion: If the sidebar_dual_implementation issue is resolved by picking one set of sidebar components, two of these three will naturally be removed. If the panel binary is also updated to use the ui-core library's mapping, only one copy needs to exist. Short of that, move the mapping into a shared function in a crate that both the binary and the ui-core library can depend on (e.g., a small file in colony-panel or a new colony-icons helper). Do not add a dependency inversion layer — a simple `pub fn file_icon(ext: &str) -> (&'static str, Color)` in the right shared crate is sufficient.

root_causes: The sidebar subsystem was apparently developed twice — once as a prompt/builtin component family (builtins/sidebar_*.rs) and once as a standalone panel family (sidebar/panels/*.rs) — without consolidating the two. This is the primary source of convention drift in the ui-core crate.

The panel binary protocol (colony-*-bin crates) evolved without a shared constants file or shared protocol helper, causing subscription key strings and error handling style to drift between sibling binaries.
likely_symptoms: filetree_bin_wrong_subscription_key is a functional symptom of the tuple_key_naming_drift root cause — it may or may not be a real bug depending on whether the panel-host broadcast path covers the use case
